sources.entry: Agent Collab Skills by Wenyu Chiou - Claude Code marketplace for multi-agent collaboration — task splitter, output reconciler, adversarial debate, shared memory, acceptance gate. Composes with codex-delegate / gemini-delegate.

summary.one_liner: A Claude Code skill bundle and optional standard-library Python harness for governing multi-agent collaboration: task splitting, debate, acceptance gating, proposal-only memory, and checkpointed policy evaluation.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides four provider-neutral skills (agent-task-splitter, agent-context-budget, agent-debate, agent-acceptance-gate) that fire on collaboration situations such as fanning out subagents, making a consequential decision between two options, or committing merged lane output. The task splitter produces a lane table with roles, model tiers, disjoint write scopes and capped returns; the debate skill runs two opposed reviewers with a round cap and passes the synthesis to a human; the acceptance gate reconciles results and returns PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, or FAIL evidence. An optional Python package, agent-collab-harness (command agent-collab), validates and evaluates machine-readable policy and checkpoint files, supports checkpoint migration and goal-slice advancement, and includes a doctor command. Memory is described as proposal-only, with canonical memory changes requiring a recorded human decision in an append-only log. The README says the skills install as a Claude Code plugin marketplace bundle.
use_cases: coordinate multiple Claude Code subagents on one goal
split work into lanes with disjoint file write scopes
get two opposing reviews before a consequential decision
gate commits or pushes on reconciled acceptance evidence
validate and evaluate agent budget policy and checkpoint files
resume an unattended multi-session agent run from a checkpoint
notable: Native mode keeps lane tables and briefs in the conversation with no files written to .coord/, while harness mode adds a policy and checkpoint contract for unattended or resumable runs
Human decisions are HMAC-bound to actions, with keys supplied by a trusted host and pinned by digest in the canonical policy
Policy evaluation fails closed when a configured policy is unreadable
Governance layer design: the host supplies models, tools, sessions and sandboxes; this project supplies roles, policy, checkpoints and evidence
Redirect stubs document migration from the removed output-reconciler, shared-memory and plan-act-reflect skills
caveats: The README describes it as a governance layer, not a general agent runtime; the host must supply models, tools and sessions
Human-authorization features need a trusted host to supply HMAC keys, and the legacy portable v1 policy shape fails closed for human records until upgraded
The README mentions Claude Code-specific mechanisms (Agent, SendMessage, Workflow, worktrees) for native lanes, so the skills are tied to that host
